q: An older adult with constipation takes verapamil, amitriptyline, and oral ferrous sulfate. Which assessment of these medications agrees with Table 87-5?
o: Consider contributions from verapamil, the tricyclic antidepressant, and the iron supplement
Consider verapamil and the tricyclic antidepressant; regard the iron supplement as protective
Consider the tricyclic antidepressant and iron supplement; regard verapamil as protective
Consider verapamil and the iron supplement; regard the tricyclic antidepressant as protective
explanation:
A medication review can uncover several independent causes of slow transit. Verapamil inhibits smooth-muscle contraction, amitriptyline has antimuscarinic activity and oral iron can cause gastrointestinal adverse effects.
**Consider all three drugs as contributors.**

**A. Verapamil, amitriptyline and iron.** Review the indication and dose of each alongside stool pattern and recent changes.
**B. Iron as protective.** Oral iron can worsen constipation, especially when poorly absorbed iron reaches the bowel.
**C. Verapamil as protective.** Verapamil is among the calcium-channel blockers most likely to slow lower-bowel motility.
**D. Amitriptyline as protective.** Blocking muscarinic receptors reduces gut smooth-muscle contractility.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1358–1359, Table 87-5.

q: מהו מבחן MRVD (מכון רפואי להערכת נהגים)?
o: מבחן מעשי ותיאורטי הכולל הערכה קוגניטיבית, ראיה, ומבחן נהיגה בכביש
שאלון עצמי בלבד
בדיקת דם
סימולטור בלבד
explanation:
המרב״ד הוא המכון הרפואי לבטיחות בדרכים. הוא בוחר בדיקות לפי סיבת ההפניה, המידע הרפואי ותפקוד הנהג, ומעביר את המלצתו לרשות הרישוי.
**מבין האפשרויות, ההערכה הרב־תחומית היא הקרובה ביותר לתהליך בפועל. הרכב הבדיקות משתנה בין נבדקים.**

**א. מבחן מעשי ותיאורטי משולב** האפשרות מזהה שהבירור בוחן כמה היבטים של הכשירות. אין מבחן אחיד המחייב בדיקת ראייה, הערכה קוגניטיבית ונהיגה בכביש אצל כל נבדק.
**ב. שאלון עצמי בלבד** דיווח עצמי עלול להחמיץ פגיעה בערנות או בשיפוט. הצוות בוחן גם נתונים רפואיים ותפקודיים.
**ג. בדיקת דם** בדיקה מעבדתית ממוקדת עשויה להשיב על שאלה קלינית. היא אינה בודקת לבדה כשירות לנהיגה.
**ד. סימולטור בלבד** גם הערכת ביצוע אינה מחליפה את בירור הבעיה הרפואית והשלכותיה.

אסמכתא · משרד הבריאות, בדיקות כשירות רפואית לנהיגה במרב״ד, סעיפים ״אילו בדיקות מבוצעות״ ו״המשך הטיפול במופנים״. חוזר מנכ״ל 6/2023, סעיפים 5–6.
Key note: משרד הבריאות מתאר יום בדיקות מותאם אישית. הניסוח באפשרות א׳ מציג בטעות נהיגה בכביש ומכלול בדיקות קבוע כחלק הכרחי מהבירור.

q: An 82-year-old frail man with heart failure and chronic kidney disease has iron-deficiency anemia (hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, ferritin 15 ng/mL). He lives in assisted living and has difficulty adhering to medications. His daughter is concerned about frequent clinic visits. Which oral iron schedule does Hazzard generally prefer for initial replacement?
o: Daily dosing, because iron improves absorption the following day
Every-other-day dosing, because iron reduces next-day absorption
Daily dosing, because iron lowers hepcidin the following day
Every-other-day dosing, because iron lowers hepcidin for two days
explanation:
Ferritin of 15 ng/mL points to depleted iron stores, even in someone who also has kidney and heart disease. Oral iron briefly limits absorption of the dose that follows it.

**For initial oral replacement, give iron every other day.**

**A. Daily because absorption improves.** The previous dose reduces next-day absorption through the hepcidin response.
**B. Every other day because absorption falls.** The intervening day separates doses while iron-induced hepcidin is elevated.
**C. Daily because hepcidin falls.** Hepcidin rises after iron administration, limiting iron entry into the blood.
**D. Every other day because hepcidin stays low.** Persistently low hepcidin would favor absorption. The reason for spacing is the temporary rise after each dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.

q: An initial anemia work-up in an older adult identifies no nutritional deficiency or impaired renal function. Which observation does Hazzard describe in studies of unexplained anemia in older adults?
o: Clonal hematopoiesis mutations account for most cases of unexplained anemia
Impaired renal excretory function characterizes the inadequate erythropoietin finding
Inadequate erythropoietin production occurs with preserved renal excretory function
Hematopoietic responses to stress become stronger as the patient grows older
explanation:
Erythropoietin is the kidney's hormonal signal for red-cell production. In some older adults the response to anemia is inappropriately small despite preserved renal excretory function.

**Insufficient erythropoietin production can occur without measurable impairment of excretory kidney function.**

**A. Clonal mutations in most cases.** Clonal hematopoiesis is only somewhat more common in anemic people than in controls and cannot explain most cases.
**B. Reduced excretory function.** The observation concerns people whose excretory function is preserved.
**C. Inadequate hormone response with preserved excretion.** Filtration and the ability to increase erythropoietin in response to anemia can differ.
**D. Stronger marrow responses with age.** Aging reduces the marrow's reserve under stress, which can slow recovery after illness or blood loss.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1480.

q: Biochemical recurrence is detected after radical prostatectomy. Which measure is useful for monitoring and deciding when to initiate treatment?
o: The passage of six months after surgery without new complaints
The PSA-doubling time assessed during follow-up after radical prostatectomy
The degree of recovery of urinary continence after surgery
The absence of local pain at a postoperative follow-up visit
explanation:
A rising PSA after prostatectomy can detect recurrent disease before symptoms appear. **PSA doubling time** quantifies the pace of biochemical recurrence and helps guide treatment timing.

**A. Six symptom-free months.** Elapsed time alone says little about how quickly recurrent disease is growing.
**B. PSA doubling time.** Serial measurements distinguish a rapid rise from a more indolent biochemical course.
**C. Urinary continence recovery.** Continence reflects postoperative function, not tumor kinetics.
**D. No local pain.** Biochemical recurrence commonly precedes local symptoms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1416.

q: Why were enhanced influenza vaccines, such as the MF59-adjuvanted vaccine, developed for older adults?
o: To broaden coverage beyond the seasonal strains in the vaccine.
To provide live-virus replication in the nasal mucosa.
To improve the weaker response to standard-dose vaccination in older adults.
To provide passive neutralizing antibodies against influenza.
explanation:
Aging can weaken the antibody response to standard-dose influenza vaccine and leave older adults less well protected. **MF59 is an adjuvant added to strengthen the immune response to vaccine antigens.**

**A. To broaden coverage beyond the seasonal strains in the vaccine** — Adjuvantation aims to improve the response to included antigens, not expand the list of strains.
**B. To provide live-virus replication in the nasal mucosa** — An MF59-adjuvanted vaccine is not a live intranasal vaccine.
**C. To improve the weaker response to standard-dose vaccination in older adults** — The adjuvant helps elicit a stronger immune response in a population with diminished responses to standard vaccination.
**D. To provide passive neutralizing antibodies against influenza** — Vaccination elicits active immunity rather than administering preformed antibodies.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1735.

q: A 78-year-old woman takes nitrofurantoin daily for long-term suppression of recurrent urinary tract infections. Her creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. According to the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, which recommendation addresses the long-term suppression?
o: Stop long-term suppression and reassess the prevention plan
Continue long-term suppression with periodic renal-function monitoring
Reduce the daily dose and continue long-term suppression
Give the dose in the evening and continue long-term suppression
explanation:
Nitrofurantoin can cause pulmonary, hepatic, or peripheral nerve toxicity, particularly with prolonged exposure.

**Stop long-term suppression and reassess prevention.** Her creatinine clearance of 42 mL/min is above the separate renal cutoff, but duration is sufficient reason to reconsider.

**A. Stop suppression.** Removing prolonged exposure addresses toxicity risk while allowing a fresh review of recurrent infection prevention.
**B. Continue and monitor kidney function.** Renal monitoring cannot remove the pulmonary, hepatic, and neurologic risks of ongoing suppression.
**C. Reduce the daily dose.** A lower daily dose still leaves her on prolonged suppressive treatment.
**D. Give it at night.** Changing the hour of dosing does not shorten exposure.

Reference · 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, p. 2057.

q: An 85-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and unstable renal function needs ventricular rate control. How does Hazzard characterize digoxin relative to first-line agents?
o: Greater effectiveness and a wide therapeutic index
Greater effectiveness and a narrow therapeutic index
Lower effectiveness and a wide therapeutic index
Lower effectiveness and a narrow therapeutic index
explanation:
Digoxin slows AV nodal conduction, but rate control can be inadequate during exertion or adrenergic stress. **It is less effective than first-line agents and has a narrow therapeutic index.**

**A. Greater effectiveness, wide index** — Both claims are reversed. Digoxin may provide incomplete rate control and can become toxic with a small rise in exposure.
**B. Greater effectiveness, narrow index** — The toxicity concern is correct. Digoxin is generally less effective than beta blockers or appropriate nodal calcium-channel blockers.
**C. Lower effectiveness, wide index** — Its limited effectiveness fits. Fluctuating renal clearance can readily move a dose into the toxic range.
**D. Lower effectiveness, narrow index** — Consider a selected role with cautious dosing and monitoring, especially when renal function changes.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1201, Rate Control.

q: בן 70, מעשן כבד, ברקע מחלת ריאות חסימתית כרונית קשה וברונכואקטזיות. בשנה האחרונה אשפוזים חוזרים עקב חום, שיעול פרודוקטיבי וקוצר נשימה. איזה טיפול אנטיביוטי מומלץ?
o: INVANZ (ERTAPENEM)
AUGMENTIN (AMOXYCILLIN + CLAVULANIC ACID)
ROCEPHINE (CEFTRIAXONE)
CIPROXIN (CIPROFLOXACIN)
explanation:
Recurrent infective exacerbations with bronchiectasis raise concern for resistant airway organisms. **Ciprofloxacin is the listed agent with antipseudomonal activity**. Prior isolates, sputum culture, severity and susceptibility determine when the other antibiotics are appropriate.

**A. Ertapenem.** It covers many resistant Enterobacterales but lacks reliable Pseudomonas activity.
**B. Amoxicillin–clavulanate.** It can cover usual COPD pathogens when resistant gram-negative organisms are unlikely.
**C. Ceftriaxone.** It is useful for many community-acquired pneumonias but misses Pseudomonas.
**D. Ciprofloxacin.** Its spectrum makes it relevant with Pseudomonas risk. Culture and clinical severity should guide selection.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1260, 1682, 1683, 1688.
Key note: All four choices were accepted. Hazzard distinguishes treatment for common respiratory organisms from treatment directed against Pseudomonas.

q: מה נכון לגבי תופעות לוואי של NSAIDS?
o: קיים סיכון קרדיו-ווסקולרי גבוה יותר ב- NSAIDS לא סלקטיבים לעומת NSAIDS סלקטיבים
טיפול בחוסמי משאבות פרוטונים (PPI) תורם להגנה מפני דימום ממערכת העיכול
לצורך הפחתת תופעות לוואי מומלץ להפחית מינון במטופלים עם פינוי קריאטינין < 30 מל/דקה
בחלק מהחולים ניתן לראות ירידת לחץ דם משנית להשפעה משתנת של התרופות
explanation:
Systemic NSAIDs inhibit prostaglandin production, which contributes to gastric injury and sodium retention as well as analgesia. **A proton-pump inhibitor reduces the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding during NSAID treatment.**

**A. Higher cardiovascular risk for all nonselective NSAIDs** — Cardiovascular risk varies by agent, dose and patient. Both selective and nonselective agents warrant caution.
**B. PPI gastroprotection** — Acid suppression reduces upper gastrointestinal ulcer and bleeding risk, although some risk remains. It provides no renal or cardiac protection.
**C. Reduce the dose below a clearance of thirty** — In advanced CKD the safer approach is to avoid systemic NSAIDs. Dose reduction alone does not remove kidney injury risk.
**D. Hypotension from diuresis** — NSAIDs impair renal sodium and water excretion. Blood pressure and congestion can worsen, particularly in heart failure.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 52, pp. 787–788, and ch. 76, p. 1173. AGS Beers Criteria 2023, Tables 2, 3 and 6.

q: מה הטיפול המתאים לפצע המופיע בתמונה מספר 3?
o: Hydrocolloids – כגון Granuflex
Hydrogels - כגון Hydrogel
Alginates – כגון Kaltostat
Hydrofibers – כגון Aquacel
explanation:
A shallow-appearing wound with little visible drainage needs moisture balance without excessive absorption. The photograph alone cannot quantify ongoing exudate, so verify drainage when the old dressing is removed.

**Hydrocolloid and hydrogel are reasonable for a wound with low to moderate drainage.** The choice depends on the actual moisture level, the surrounding skin and the need to cover or hydrate the bed.

**A. Hydrocolloid.** A wafer can retain moisture, support autolysis and absorb low to moderate exudate.
**B. Hydrogel.** A high-water-content gel maintains a moist bed, supports autolysis and can cool painful tissue.
**C. Alginate.** Its stronger absorption suits moderate to heavy drainage. Alginate can dry out a wound with little exudate.
**D. Hydrofiber.** These dressings gel as they absorb wound fluid and suit greater drainage. The pictured wound gives no clear reason to choose this capacity.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 693–694, Table 46-2.

q: Describe regurgitation compatible with normal aging.
o: Trivial or mild central regurgitation with leaflets appearing normal for age
Severe central regurgitation with leaflets appearing normal for the patient’s age
Trivial or mild central regurgitation with leaflets showing major structural abnormalities
Moderate central regurgitation with leaflets appearing normal for the patient’s age
explanation:
A small central regurgitant jet can occur with age-related valve or annular changes. **Trivial or mild central regurgitation with leaflets normal for age** fits a physiologic aging pattern.

**A. Trivial or mild and normal leaflets.** Both severity and morphology are compatible.
**B. Severe central regurgitation.** Severity warrants assessment for pathology despite a central jet.
**C. Abnormal leaflets.** Major structural disease requires its own explanation even with a small jet.
**D. Moderate central regurgitation.** Moderate leakage exceeds the expected aging pattern.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1120.

q: An incidentally detected adrenal mass is homogeneous on unenhanced CT. Which attenuation is the current ESE criterion for a benign imaging phenotype requiring no further imaging?
o: At or below 5 HU only
Above 20 HU only
At or below 10 HU
At or above 30 HU
explanation:
A homogeneous lesion measuring 10 HU or less on noncontrast CT has a benign imaging phenotype. This imaging decision is separate from appropriate hormonal assessment and from management of heterogeneous lesions.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch97; European Society of Endocrinology adrenal incidentaloma guideline, 2023.

בן 80, מאושפז במחלקה פנימית גריאטרית עקב זיהום בדרכי בשתן. המטופל נשא קתטר שתן קבוע מזה שנתיים.
ביום השני של האשפוז עבר בדיקת CT בטן עם חומר ניגוד ונשלל אבצס.
ביום השלישי לאשפוזו הוחל טיפול אנטיביוטי ב- Amikacin לפי רגישות החיידק.
במהלך האשפוז החום ירד, ללא דהידרציה, לחץ דם יציב ותפוקת שתן תקינה.
ביום העשירי לאשפוז קריאטינין עלה מ-1 עד 3.
מה מהבאים יתמוך באבחנה של אי ספיקת כליות משנית לטיפול באמינוגלוקוזידים?

explanation:
Aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity usually causes tubular injury after several days and can preserve urine output. **Granular casts in the urine sediment** support this mechanism after a week of amikacin.

**A. BUN-to-creatinine ratio above 20.** This can suggest reduced effective perfusion and is not specific for tubular toxicity.
**B. Oliguria.** Aminoglycoside injury is frequently nonoliguric, so preserved urine output does not exclude it.
**C. Granular casts.** These reflect tubular injury and fit both the exposure and timing.
**D. Hypermagnesemia.** Aminoglycosides can cause tubular magnesium wasting, tending toward hypomagnesemia.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 2377, 2380.
